title: cohort-lattice-and-shadow-absorber-with-rollback-oracle
author: Lina Zhao
release_notes: Adds a cohort-lattice orchestration primitive and an asynchronous shadow-absorber for non-blocking shadow traffic observation. Introduces a rollback-oracle that grades cohorts and triggers preemptive swapback when safety gates are violated.
description:
Motivation: large staged rollouts currently either block on synchronous shadow verification (increasing p95 latency) or sample too sparsely and miss regressions. This PR introduces a cohort-lattice orchestration primitive plus an asynchronous shadow-absorber process that decouples shadow capture from request latency while preserving per-cohort signal fidelity. It also wires a lightweight rollback-oracle that can preemptively trigger an automated rollback when multiple safety gates (latency, error-rate, token-quality regression) cross thresholds simultaneously.

What changed (high-level): Implemented cohort-lattice controller: a DAG-based cohort graph that supports overlapping cohorts and weighted joins; implemented shadow-absorber: an async consumer that persists shadow pairs (request+candidate responses) to a bounded ring buffer and performs deterministic downstream comparison without impacting live latency; added rollback-oracle service that consumes cohort metrics and eval signals to decide immediate preemption vs. delayed rollback. Added metrics, tracing hooks, and playbook links.

Commits summary: - 9bd1f3c: implement cohort-lattice data model and scheduler - 1f7a22e: async shadow-absorber worker + bounded ring buffer + backpressure handling - 4c3b5a1: rollback-oracle evaluation rules and scoreboard - ae2f11d: telemetry: prometheus metrics and tracing spans - bc9d2e4: unit and integration tests for cohort transitions - d4f8a11: docs + runbook + console wiring

Changed areas / files (illustrative): - rollout/controller/lattice.go (new) - rollout/absorber/worker.go (new) - rollout/oracle/oracle.go (new) - rollout/tests/integration_lattice_test.go (new) - console/rollouts.vue (patched) - telemetry/metrics_rollouts.prom (patched) - docs/runbooks/rollback-oracle.md (new) - charts/values-rollout.yaml (patched)

Small diff snippet (short illustrative extract): "diff --git a/rollout/absorber/worker.go b/rollout/absorber/worker.go
+ func processShadow(ctx context.Context, req *Request, candidate *Response) {
+   // enqueue non-blocking, drop-on-full with counter increments for observability
+   if !ringBuffer.TryEnqueue(shadowPair{Req: req, Cand: candidate}) {
+       metrics.RolloutShadowDrop.Inc()
+   }
+ }"

Tests and CI: initial CI run failed on one flaky integration asserting cohort transition timing (integration_lattice_test.go). I reproduced locally, adjusted the test to tolerate scheduler jitter and added a deterministic hook that can be toggled under TEST_MODE. After that fix CI passed on the second run. Full CI summary: unit tests: pass, integration: pass (after rerun), lint: pass, e2e-smoke: pass.

Review conversation highlights (condensed): - Marcus Liu: requested clearer invariants for cohort join/leave semantics; asked for explicit guarantees when cohorts overlap. Response: added explicit invariants to lattice.go docstring and unit tests that assert invariant retention during concurrent transitions. - Evelyn Grant: asked about backpressure behavior when absorber ring is full during spikes. Response: implemented drop-on-full policy and counters, added integration test that simulates bursty traffic and verifies graceful degradation (metrics emitted). - Rahul Kapoor: recommended making rollback-oracle decision rules declarative and pluggable. Response: extracted rule engine interface and shipped a default rule set; left TODO and an interface for customers to provide custom evaluators (in future PR).

Operational notes and runbook: added docs/runbooks/rollback-oracle.md with decision flow, thresholds used in default config, and manual override steps in the console. The default rollout policy enables async shadow-absorber for cohorts tagged with "async-shadow=true"; teams can opt-in per-rollout. The rollback-oracle defaults to conservative thresholds (5% relative latency regressions OR 2x error-rate within a 5m window combined with token-quality drift > 3 points triggers preemptive rollback).

Migration and compatibility: changes are backward compatible. Existing rollout definitions continue to work; a new optional "cohortLattice" stanza enables advanced overlap semantics. Rollback-oracle can be disabled via configs for teams that prefer manual remediation.

Merge outcome: squash-merged to main on 2026-02-24 after approvals from Marcus and Evelyn and green CI. Post-merge: deployed to canary region with a light traffic gate (5% global) then progressively enabled per-team opt-ins. Observability: added cohort-scoped dashboards and alerting rules under telemetry/alerts-rollouts.yaml.

Related work and follow-ups: - ENG-4821 (linear): dashboarding for per-cohort token-quality regressions - ENG-4980: formalizing custom rollback-evaluator plugin API - follow-up PR planned to add deterministic replay tooling that converts ring-buffered shadow pairs into replay jobs for staged offline evaluation.

Notes for reviewers: this PR touches control-plane orchestration and a small runtime worker. Please pay attention to concurrency invariants in lattice.go and the backpressure counters in absorber/worker.go. If you prefer a more conservative default for drop-on-full behavior, we can change policy via values-rollout.yaml before wide rollout.
